headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API/network access can leak or act on LlamaFactory-generated content, while LlamaFactory itself has no runtime surfaces to constrain the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no runtime I/O surfaces, filesystem access, or MCP, so it cannot ingest RD-Agent output by default. RD-Agent can browse and call APIs, but there is no documented shared channel between them. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore blocked by the profiles as given.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies RD-Agent output into a LlamaFactory prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not bridge them with copy-paste workflows.
Disable any shared workspace or queue.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, logs, execution traces, and secrets-backed APIs, and it has broad network egress. LlamaFactory itself has no data-touching surfaces, so it is not the leak source; the risk is that RD-Agent can exfiltrate sensitive research data to third-party APIs during normal operation. The pair increases exposure because one agent is data-rich and the other is unconstrained by the profiles.
conditions: IF RD-Agent is given financial reports or logs containing sensitive content, leakage risk is present.
IF RD-Agent is configured to send prompts or traces to external APIs, data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive datasets.
Rotate or scope API keys to least privilege.
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Review log/ directory contents before execution.
requires-engineering: route sensitive workloads through a local-only model stack.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with RD-Agent. RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, but the pair lacks overlapping write surfaces in the profiles. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory is introduced, file contention becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator gives LlamaFactory write permissions not listed here, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only.
Separate log directories per agent.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Run one instance per workspace.
requires-engineering: add file locks around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can act on outputs via APIs and browser access, while LlamaFactory is a model/fine-tuning tool with no verification or downstream action controls in the profile. If LlamaFactory-generated text is fed into RD-Agent, RD-Agent may treat it as authoritative and propagate errors into research actions or API calls. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory output is used as input to RD-Agent without verification, errors can cascade.
IF RD-Agent is allowed to execute browser/API actions based on model output, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review before RD-Agent acts.
Add a verification step between agents.
Use structured schemas for transferred outputs.
Log and diff all handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before any action-taking step.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports and logs and uses third-party APIs, creating residency and retention concerns. LlamaFactory is open-source and has no documented data handling, so it is not the compliance driver here. The pair is risky because RD-Agent’s default external API usage can move regulated data outside the operator’s intended boundary.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by RD-Agent, external API use may create a residency or retention mismatch.
IF the operator requires local-only processing, RD-Agent’s default egress violates that requirement.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from RD-Agent runs.
Use a local-only model endpoint.
Review API retention settings.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
